description: AWS RDS Aurora PostgreSQL telemetry from the AWS/RDS CloudWatch namespace (RED method, then saturation and limits), the postgresql log export, account usage against service quotas, and optional Performance Insights and Enhanced Monitoring rows.

panels.description: Storage used by the cluster volume. Drives storage billing. Collected at intervals: keep the period at 5m or more. Limit: 128 TiB per cluster, 256 TiB from Aurora PostgreSQL 17.5, 16.9, and 15.13 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_Limits.html). https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Volume storage used ($period)

panels.description: Billed read and write I/O operations on the cluster volume, reported per 5 minutes. Divide by 300 for operations per second. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Billed volume IOPs (5 minutes)

panels.description: Backup storage inside the retention window, snapshot storage outside it, and the billed total. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Backup storage ($period)

panels.description: Commit operations per second. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Commit throughput ($period)

panels.description: Read operations per second and Aurora storage write records per second. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Disk IOPS ($period)

panels.description: Bytes read from and written to storage per second. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Disk throughput ($period)

panels.description: Traffic between clients and the instance, storage traffic excluded. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Client network throughput ($period)

panels.description: Traffic between the instance and the Aurora storage subsystem. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Storage network throughput ($period)

panels.description: Client network connections per role against the max_connections parameter, drawn from the max_connections variable. Default max_connections = LEAST(DBInstanceClassMemory/9531392, 5000): 450 for db.t4g.medium (4 GiB). The READER series sums every reader of the cluster. When hit, new clients get FATAL remaining connection slots are reserved: see the Error logs panel. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.Managing.html#AuroraPostgreSQL.Managing.MaxConnections
panels.title: Database connections ($period)

panels.description: Deadlocks per second, summed over the period. Any value is a bug in the application's lock order. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Deadlocks ($period)

panels.description: PostgreSQL log export filtered on error severities and on connection refusals (remaining connection slots, too many connections), the only signal Aurora emits when max_connections is hit. Needs enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["postgresql"]. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.CloudWatch.Logs.html

targets.expression:
fields @timestamp, @message, @logStream
| filter @message like /ERROR|FATAL|PANIC|deadlock|canceling statement|remaining connection slots|too many connections/
| sort @timestamp desc
| display @timestamp, @message

panels.title: Error logs

panels.description: Average duration of commit operations across engine and storage. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Commit latency ($period)

panels.description: Average time per disk I/O operation. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Disk I/O latency ($period)

panels.description: Lag between the writer and each reader. Empty on a single-instance cluster. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Replica lag ($period)

panels.description: Percentage of CPU used by the instance. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: CPU utilization ($period)

panels.description: Burstable classes only (db.t3, db.t4g), reported every 5 minutes. The balance caps at the credits earned over 24 hours: 576 for db.t4g.medium (24 per hour), so a flat line at the cap means the instance never bursts. A balance at zero means the instance runs at baseline; charged surplus credits cost money. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/burstable-credits-baseline-concepts.html https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: CPU credits ($period)

panels.description: Available RAM, swap in use, and the shared buffer memory actively used. Swap above zero means the working set no longer fits. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Memory ($period)

panels.description: Local storage left for temporary tables and sorts. Limit per instance class: 8.13 GiB for db.t4g.medium, 16.5 GiB for db.t4g.large (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.Managing.html#AuroraPostgreSQL.Managing.TempStorage). Zero fails sorts and index builds. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Free local storage ($period)

panels.description: Outstanding I/O requests waiting for the disk. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Disk queue depth ($period)

panels.description: Share of requests served by the buffer cache. A fall means reads spill to storage and billed IOPs rise. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Buffer cache hit ratio ($period)

panels.description: Age of the oldest unvacuumed transaction ID. At 2,146,483,648 PostgreSQL goes read-only to avoid wraparound. Check autovacuum when it climbs. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Transaction ID age ($period)

panels.description: Logical replication only. TransactionLogsDiskUsage reads -1 when transaction logs are not in use. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Replication slots and transaction logs ($period)

panels.description: Time since the engine started. A drop marks a restart or a failover. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMySQL.Monitoring.Metrics.html
panels.title: Engine uptime ($period)

panels.description: PostgreSQL log export of the selected cluster. The filter box narrows on a substring. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.CloudWatch.Logs.html

targets.expression:
fields @timestamp, @message, @logStream
| filter strcontains(@message, "$log_filter")
| sort @timestamp desc
| display @timestamp, @message

panels.title: PostgreSQL

panels.description: Account-level resource counts from the AWS/Usage namespace. Creating a resource past its quota fails with an exception. Quotas: DBClusters https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-952B80B8 (default 40), DBInstances https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-7B6409FD (default 40), ManualClusterSnapshots https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-9B510759 (default 100), DBSubnetGroups https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-48C6BF61 (default 50), ReadReplicasPerMaster https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-5BC124EF (default 15). https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_Limits.html
panels.title: RDS resource counts ($period)

panels.description: Percent of each applied quota used, from the SERVICE_QUOTA metric math function. Above 80 request an increase in the Service Quotas console: DBClusters https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-952B80B8 (default 40), DBInstances https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-7B6409FD (default 40), ManualClusterSnapshots https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-9B510759 (default 100), DBSubnetGroups https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-48C6BF61 (default 50), ReadReplicasPerMaster https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/rds/quotas/L-5BC124EF (default 15). https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Usage-Metrics.html
panels.title: Quota utilization ($period)

panels.description: Average active sessions, split between CPU and non-CPU wait events. Published only under load and only with Performance Insights enabled. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_PerfInsights.Cloudwatch.html
panels.title: DB load ($period)

panels.description: DB load divided by the vCPU count. Above 1 the instance has more active sessions than cores. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_PerfInsights.Cloudwatch.html
panels.title: DB load per vCPU ($period)
Performance Insights (optional: Database Insights standard mode, free for 7 days retention)

panels.description: OS-level CPU from the RDSOSMetrics log group. Paid: CloudWatch Logs ingestion at the chosen granularity. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_Monitoring.OS.html

targets.expression:
fields @timestamp, instanceID, cpuUtilization.total as total, cpuUtilization.user as user, cpuUtilization.system as sys, cpuUtilization.wait as wait
| filter instanceID like /^$db_cluster-/
| stats avg(total) as cpu_total, avg(user) as cpu_user, avg(sys) as cpu_system, avg(wait) as cpu_wait by bin($period)

panels.title: OS CPU ($period)

panels.description: OS-level memory in kilobytes from the RDSOSMetrics log group. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_Monitoring.OS.html

targets.expression:
fields @timestamp, instanceID, memory.free as free, memory.cached as cached, memory.active as active, swap.free as swapfree
| filter instanceID like /^$db_cluster-/
| stats avg(free) as mem_free, avg(cached) as mem_cached, avg(active) as mem_active, avg(swapfree) as swap_free by bin($period)

panels.title: OS memory ($period)

panels.description: Load averages and task states from the RDSOSMetrics log group. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_Monitoring.OS.html

targets.expression:
fields @timestamp, instanceID, loadAverageMinute.one as l1, loadAverageMinute.five as l5, loadAverageMinute.fifteen as l15, tasks.running as running, tasks.blocked as blocked
| filter instanceID like /^$db_cluster-/
| stats avg(l1) as load_1m, avg(l5) as load_5m, avg(l15) as load_15m, max(running) as tasks_running, max(blocked) as tasks_blocked by bin($period)

panels.title: Load average and tasks ($period)
Enhanced Monitoring (optional: paid CloudWatch Logs ingestion)

list.description: max_connections of the selected instance. Default LEAST(DBInstanceClassMemory/9531392, 5000): 450 for db.t4g.medium. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.Managing.html#AuroraPostgreSQL.Managing.MaxConnections
list.label: max_connections
list.name: max_connections

title: AWS RDS CloudWatch
